title.narrative: OHCHR - Human Rights Monitoring Mission to Ukraine (HRMMU) - 2025-28

description.narrative:
The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission to Ukraine (HRMMU) has been deployed since 2014 to monitor and protect the human rights of women, men, girls and boys across all of Ukraine, including territory occupied by the Russian Federation.
The mission works to ensure that human rights concerns are integrated into UN and partner plans (humanitarian response, recovery/reconstruction, conflict management), and are taken up by relevant international actors in a timely manner. Accountability and protection are supported through HRMMU’s evidence base, leading to investigations, prosecutorial guidance/policy change, judicial reliance on findings, and improved treatment/conditions for POWs and detainees.
HRMMU will enhance monitoring of vulnerable groups to ensure that the differential impacts of the conflict are understood and addressed. Special attention to women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and religious and ethnic minorities will inform targeted protection strategies and contribute to more inclusive recovery planning.
The major focus of the HRMMU work is aimed at documentation of violations and advocacy related to the promotion of economic, social, and cultural rights with focus on needs of women, older persons, persons with disabilities, minorities, and children. HRMMU will also pay special attention to the rights of women and persons in especially vulnerable situations or facing discrimination, such as people living in isolated communities near the front line, persons with disabilities, and minority groups, as these groups have been disproportionally affected by the conflict. HRMMU also documents and verifies allegations of conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV). One of the activities under the project is the publication of a report on the human rights situation in Ukraine with attention to conflict-related and gender-based violations.
